attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post, in his own voice and not quoting anyone else.

semantics.note: A faithful, unhedged present-tense observation. 'Essentially no regulation' keeps the meaning of 'essentially zero' and covers all three areas he named.

contract.note: The plain reading is fair and ordinary. A US focus follows from his appeal to Congress, 'essentially' allows minor exceptions, and general deception law alone does not count against him. The result still depends on the inferred jurisdiction and on where the line falls between chatbot-specific duties and general law.

evidence.note: Official California history published before the evaluation date. It says the state had no law aimed specifically at companion chatbots before 2025. That fits the claim, but it covers one state and does not settle the national position or other applicable duties.
A 2025 CRS report finding no broad federal AI legislation. It does not rule out narrower federal duties governing chatbot behaviour in February 2023.

A February 2023 Italian regulator action restricting Replika over risks to vulnerable users. It qualifies a worldwide reading, but it concerns Italy and data-protection law, not US behavioural requirements.

reviews.rationale: Under the US-focused plain reading, the packet leans toward Marcus: California had no companion-chatbot-specific law and there was no broad federal AI statute. But no source establishes the nationwide US position on February 22, 2023, or rules out applicable duties or enforcement. Key sources could not be read. The Italian action is outside the inferred jurisdiction. The evidence does not settle the outcome.
